newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador bond allocation stronger after rating.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador bond allocation stronger after rating.

text.p: Ecuador's government said Friday the auction of short-term bonds a day earlier was the strongest sign yet of the positive impact of the recent credit rating assigned to the country's debt by Moody's Investors Service.
"The rating given to Ecuador had decisive influence on the result of the auction, which shows the new levels of confidence offered by the country," said a statement from the Finance Ministry.
Moody's rated Ecuador's long-term foreign currency debt at B1, putting it at the same level as Argentina and Brazil.
Thursday's auction of $20.5 million of five-year bonds drew offers worth $110.73 million. The bonds were sold at a price of 101,347 for a yield of 8.88 percent.
((--Franz Bastidas, Quito Newsroom, 5932 258429 e- mail: reuters1@reutersecu.com.ec))
